reuse.why: Reuses the existing tolerance helper and API amount helper, but posting, action synchronization, and previews retain dispatch logic already owned by getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: Three consumers retain separate missing/number/range dispatch blocks instead of delegating the complete decision to getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, tolerance remains in shared/rules, and API field projection stays in api-models.

scope.why: The changes are confined to schedule amount policy, its consumers, API exposure, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Multiple overlapping amount helpers and optional operator propagation leave maintainers coordinating policy across consumers rather than relying on one complete abstraction.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts:updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, plus shared/schedules.ts:computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, bypass getScheduledAmount and retain their own dispatch.

disguised_duplication.where: Replacing midpoint arithmetic with getRangedAmount leaves duplicated missing/number/range decisions in updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter, getWorstCaseAmount adds an isapprox branch, and three consumers retain local dispatch; API conversion and existing UI callers also omit the operator needed by the expanded policy.
